title: ADscan PRO licence register export v1
description: The output of `adscan license register export` (JSON form): what one engine installation recorded under its PRO licence, for the quarterly reconciliation between a partner and ADscan. It never carries a domain name, a host, a user or a finding: a domain is its one-way per-partner domain code. entries is one row per domain code (registered rows carry the licence server's signed receipt, which verifies independently of the exporter; pending rows are a declaration). assessments is one usage line per assessment of a code: run_kind full_scan or recheck, the run, for a recheck the scan it re-checked, the identity band, the date and, from 1.1, how a full scan ended (run_status) and the size counts of each domain of the code it assessed (domain_sizes: counts only, never a name, host, address or finding). engagements is what those lines count as under the licence's retest window: a recheck never opens an engagement; a full scan inside the window of the engagement already open for its code is a retest of it; at or after the window's end it opens a new one. The licence server counts its own records with the same rule. Written by one writer (register_export in adscan_core/pro_license/client.py). Version marker: schema_version, '1.<minor>'; adscan_register is the legacy integer marker kept for readers of the first export. Declared objects may gain fields within a major; do not reject unknown keys. receipt and usage are opaque.

unattached_rechecks.$comment: Run ids of rechecks whose code has no engagement in this register (a workspace assessed before the licence was activated). Never billable.

usage.$comment: Offline engagement licences only: the environment ledger's usage for the licence term.

parent_run_id.$comment: For a recheck, the run id of the scan it re-checked; null for a full scan.

band.$comment: Identity band; pending until counted at the end of the scan.

retest_window_days.$comment: The licence window in force when a full scan ran; null for a recheck.

run_status.$comment: 1.1. How the full scan ended, in the coverage.json vocabulary: complete, partial (it ended without completing its assessment, an operator stop included) or interrupted (it never reached its end; also what the line reads while the run is still going). Null on a recheck and on a line written before 1.1. Informational: billing follows the retest window, so a relaunch of a scan that did not finish is a retest of the same engagement.

domain_sizes.$comment: 1.1. One entry per domain of this code (a forest) the run assessed, largest first, with no identifier. Null when the line has no counts (a recheck, a line written before 1.1, or a run that never reached its scan end).

domain_size.$comment: 1.1. Counts only. null means the run did not count it (the phase did not run, was skipped by the policy, or the scan stopped first); 0 means it counted and found none.

users_total.$comment: Live user objects in the directory (deleted objects excluded).

users_enabled.$comment: Enabled user accounts: the count the identity band is computed from.

computers_total.$comment: Live computer objects in the directory (deleted objects excluded).

computers_total_servers.$comment: Live computers whose operatingSystem names a server SKU (domain controllers included).

computers_total_workstations.$comment: Live computers whose operatingSystem names a Windows client edition.

computers_total_os_unknown.$comment: Live computers with no operatingSystem or one that is neither. The three add up to computers_total.

computers_enabled.$comment: Enabled computer objects in the directory.

computers_enabled_servers.$comment: Enabled computers on a server SKU (domain controllers included).

computers_enabled_workstations.$comment: Enabled computers on a Windows client edition.

computers_enabled_os_unknown.$comment: Enabled computers with no or an unrecognised operatingSystem. The three add up to computers_enabled.

computers_enabled_tier0_direct.$comment: Enabled computers placed in Tier 0 (direct) by membership or role: domain controllers and members of the groups that control the domain.

computers_enabled_tier0_escalation_capab.$comment: Enabled computers placed in Tier 0 (escalation-capable) by membership: members of a Tier 0 group one step from control of the domain, such as a certificate server in Cert Publishers.

computers_enabled_tier1.$comment: Enabled computers placed in Tier 1 by their role: member servers, by operating system or by the service they publish.

computers_enabled_tier2.$comment: Enabled computers placed in Tier 2: workstations and every computer no membership or role places higher.

computers_enabled_tier_by_right.$comment: Enabled computers placed by a permission, not by membership or role. Counted here only, never also in a tier.

computers_enabled_tier_unknown.$comment: Enabled computers with no tier. The six tier counts add up to computers_enabled; all six are null when the run's directory data carries no tiers.

computers_resolving.$comment: Enabled computers that resolved to an address the reachability pass probed.

computers_reachable.$comment: Enabled computers that answered the reachability pass (a discovery response or an open port).

domain_controllers.$comment: Domain controllers, writable and read-only, among the live computer objects.

certificate_authorities.$comment: Enterprise certificate authorities. Forest-wide objects: every domain of one forest reports the same figure, so never add them across a forest's domains.

computers_in_asset_scope.$comment: Since 1.2 filled when the run had an asset scope (an allow or deny list of hosts and directory objects): enabled computers the scope leaves in, the denominator of the report's network-reach statement. Null when the run had no asset scope, or did not list the domain's enabled computers.

computers_excluded_by_asset_scope.$comment: Since 1.2 filled when the run had an asset scope: enabled computers the scope excludes (a deny entry, or an allow list that does not cover them). They were not contacted. 0 when the scope excluded none. Null when the run had no asset scope, or did not list the domain's enabled computers.

computers_asset_scope_unconfirmed.$comment: Since 1.2 filled when the run had an asset scope: enabled computers that could not be confirmed as within the scope and were left alone. With the two counts above they add up to the enabled computers the run counted against the scope. Null when the run had no asset scope, or did not list the domain's enabled computers.

retest_until.$comment: First instant at which a full scan of the code opens a new engagement.
